source.text: Ἐν ἐκείνῳ τῷ καιρῷ ἤκουσεν Ἡρῴδης ὁ τετραάρχης τὴν ἀκοὴν Ἰησοῦ, καὶ εἶπεν τοῖς παισὶν αὐτοῦ· Οὗτός ἐστιν Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτιστής· αὐτὸς ἠγέρθη ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο αἱ δυνάμεις ἐνεργοῦσιν ἐν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: At that the time heard Herod the tetrarch the report of Jesus, \v 2 and he said to the servants of him, This is John the Baptist; he was raised from the dead, and because of this the powers are working in him.

en.L: At that time Herod the tetrarch heard the report about Jesus, \v 2 and he said to his servants, "This is John the Baptist. He has been raised from the dead, and because of this the powers are at work in him."
en.B: Around that time, reports about Jesus reached Herod the tetrarch. \v 2 "This is John the Baptist," he told his courtiers. "He has been raised from the dead, and that is why he can do these mighty works."
en.R: At that time Herod, the ruler of Galilee, heard what people were saying about Jesus. \v 2 He said to his servants, "This man is really John the Baptist! John has come back from the dead. That is why he has the power to do these miracles."

es.L: En aquel tiempo oyó Herodes el tetrarca lo que se decía de Jesús, \v 2 y dijo a sus siervos: «Este es Juan el Bautista. Él ha sido resucitado de entre los muertos, y por eso los poderes actúan en él».
es.B: Por aquel tiempo llegaron a Herodes el tetrarca noticias acerca de Jesús. \v 2 «Este es Juan el Bautista», dijo a sus cortesanos. «Ha sido resucitado de entre los muertos, y por eso puede hacer estas obras poderosas».
es.R: En ese tiempo, Herodes, el gobernante de Galilea, oyó lo que la gente decía de Jesús. \v 2 Les dijo a sus sirvientes: «¡Este hombre es en realidad Juan el Bautista! Juan ha vuelto de entre los muertos. Por eso tiene poder para hacer estos milagros».

fr.L: En ce temps-là, Hérode le tétrarque entendit la renommée de Jésus, \v 2 et il dit à ses serviteurs : « C’est Jean le Baptiste ; il est ressuscité des morts, et c’est pour cela que les puissances agissent en lui. »
fr.B: Vers ce temps-là, Hérode le tétrarque entendit parler de Jésus. \v 2 « C’est Jean le Baptiste, dit-il à ses courtisans. Il est ressuscité des morts, et voilà pourquoi il peut accomplir ces œuvres puissantes. »
fr.R: À ce moment-là, Hérode, qui gouvernait la Galilée, a entendu ce que les gens disaient de Jésus. \v 2 Il a dit à ses serviteurs : « Cet homme, c’est en fait Jean le Baptiste ! Jean est revenu d’entre les morts. Voilà pourquoi il a le pouvoir de faire ces miracles. »

sw.L: Wakati ule Herode mtawala alisikia habari za Yesu, \v 2 akawaambia watumishi wake, "Huyu ni Yohana Mbatizaji. Yeye amefufuliwa kutoka kwa wafu, na kwa sababu hiyo nguvu hizi zinatenda kazi ndani yake."
sw.B: Wakati huo habari za Yesu zilimfikia Herode mtawala. \v 2 Akawaambia watu wa baraza lake, "Huyu ni Yohana Mbatizaji. Amefufuliwa kutoka kwa wafu, ndiyo sababu anaweza kufanya matendo haya ya nguvu."
sw.R: Wakati huo Herode, mtawala wa Galilaya, alisikia mambo ambayo watu walikuwa wakisema kuhusu Yesu. \v 2 Akawaambia watumishi wake, "Mtu huyu kwa kweli ni Yohana Mbatizaji! Yohana amerudi kutoka kwa wafu. Ndiyo maana ana uwezo wa kufanya miujiza hii."

vi.L: Vào thời ấy, tiểu vương Hê-rốt nghe tin đồn về Đức Giê-xu, \v 2 và nói với các bề tôi của mình: "Người này là Giăng Báp-tít; ông ấy đã sống lại từ cõi chết, và vì thế các quyền năng đang hành động trong ông ấy."
vi.B: Vào khoảng thời gian ấy, tiểu vương Hê-rốt nghe tin đồn về Đức Giê-xu. \v 2 Ông ta nói với các triều thần: "Đây là Giăng Báp-tít. Ông ấy đã sống lại từ cõi chết, vì thế mà ông ấy làm được những việc quyền năng này."
vi.R: Lúc ấy, Hê-rốt, người cai trị Ga-li-lê, nghe người ta nói về Đức Giê-xu. \v 2 Ông ta nói với các đầy tớ của mình: "Người này chính là Giăng Báp-tít! Giăng đã sống lại từ cõi chết. Vì thế ông ấy mới có quyền năng làm những phép lạ này."

decisions.choice: Herod the tetrarch: Herod Antipas, son of Herod the Great, ruler of Galilee and Perea
decisions.reason: Herod the Great had died (2:19). His son Antipas ruled Galilee and Perea under Rome from 4 BC to AD 39. A tetrarch was a ruler of part of a kingdom, below the rank of king.

decisions.choice: at that time: a loose link to the events just told
decisions.reason: Matthew uses the phrase to join stories without fixing a date (11:25; 12:1).

decisions.choice: he has been raised: Herod thinks John has come back to life, and that this explains Jesus's mighty works
alternatives: Herod means Jesus has the same spirit as John
decisions.reason: John did no miracles (compare John 10:41), so Herod explains the powers at work in Jesus by a return from the dead. His words also show a troubled conscience, as the story that follows explains. The passive points to God as the one who raises.

decisions.choice: servants: the officials and attendants of his court
decisions.reason: The word can mean child or servant; here it is the people who serve at Herod's court.

decisions.choice: mighty works (B); miracles (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the powers". Balanced and Readable say what the powers were: the miracles Jesus was doing (11:20-23).

decisions.choice: the ruler of Galilee
decisions.reason: "Tetrarch" is unfamiliar; Readable says what Herod ruled that matters in Matthew's story.

decisions.choice: el tetrarca (L, B); el gobernante de Galilea (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: the title says that Herod Antipas ruled only part of his father's kingdom (meaning decision m1). Spanish has the word "tetrarca"; Readable says what he ruled.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); historic presents kept at Literal (14:8, 14:17)
decisions.reason: As the style guide (section 3) and Mark 6: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Readable tells the story in the passé composé, as French is spoken. The flashback (14:3-12) is in the plus-que-parfait where the English has "had". Speech keeps its own tenses. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: "les puissances" (L); "ces œuvres puissantes" (B); "ces miracles" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the plural noun, as at Mark 6:14; Balanced uses the same "œuvres puissantes" as at 13:54 and 13:58.

decisions.choice: Herode mtawala (L, B); Herode, mtawala wa Galilaya (R)
decisions.reason: The title says that Herod Antipas ruled only part of his father's kingdom (meaning decision m1). Swahili has no word for it; "mtawala" (ruler) keeps him apart from "mfalme" (king), the looser title the story gives him in verse 9, and Readable names his territory, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "tiểu vương Hê-rốt" (L, B); "Hê-rốt, người cai trị Ga-li-lê" (R) for Herod the tetrarch
decisions.reason: The word used for Herod Antipas in the Vietnamese Luke (3:1, 3:19), a ruler under Rome below a king (meaning decision); Readable says what he ruled.

decisions.choice: "ông ta" for Herod, "ông", "ông ấy" for John (14:1-12)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 6:14-29: John, the righteous prophet, is "ông"; Herod is "ông ta", a little more distant, which keeps it clear who does what.

decisions.choice: "các bề tôi" (L); "các triều thần" (B); "các đầy tớ" (R)
decisions.reason: The officials and attendants of his court (meaning decision); Balanced names them as courtiers, Readable plainly as servants.

source.text: Ὁ γὰρ Ἡρῴδης κρατήσας τὸν Ἰωάννην ἔδησεν αὐτὸν καὶ ἐν φυλακῇ ἀπέθετο διὰ Ἡρῳδιάδα τὴν γυναῖκα Φιλίππου τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ, ἔλεγεν γὰρ αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰωάννης· Οὐκ ἔξεστίν σοι ἔχειν αὐτήν·

records.literal_gloss: For Herod having seized John bound him and in prison put [him] because of Herodias the wife of Philip the brother of him; \v 4 was saying for John to him, Not it is lawful for you to have her.

en.L: For Herod, having seized John, had bound him and put [him] away in prison because of Herodias, the wife of Philip his brother; \v 4 for John had been saying to him, "It is not lawful for you to have her."
en.B: Herod had earlier arrested John, put him in chains and locked him in prison. He did it for the sake of Herodias, who had been the wife of his brother Philip. \v 4 John had told Herod again and again, "The law does not allow you to have her."
en.R: Some time before this, Herod had arrested John. He tied him up and put him in prison. Herod did this because of Herodias. She had been the wife of Herod's brother Philip, but Herod had taken her as his own wife. \v 4 John kept telling Herod, "God's law says you must not marry her!"

es.L: Porque Herodes, habiendo apresado a Juan, lo había atado y [lo] había puesto en la cárcel a causa de Herodías, esposa de su hermano Felipe; \v 4 pues Juan le había estado diciendo: «No te está permitido tenerla».
es.B: Herodes había arrestado antes a Juan, lo había encadenado y encerrado en la cárcel. Lo hizo por Herodías, que había sido la esposa de su hermano Felipe. \v 4 Juan le había dicho a Herodes una y otra vez: «La ley no te permite tenerla».
es.R: Algún tiempo antes, Herodes había arrestado a Juan. Lo ató y lo metió en la cárcel. Herodes hizo esto por causa de Herodías. Ella había sido la esposa de Felipe, el hermano de Herodes, pero Herodes la había tomado como su propia esposa. \v 4 Juan le repetía a Herodes: «¡La ley de Dios dice que no debes casarte con ella!».

fr.L: Car Hérode, ayant saisi Jean, l’avait lié et mis en prison à cause d’Hérodiade, la femme de Philippe son frère ; \v 4 car Jean lui disait : « Il ne t’est pas permis de l’avoir. »
fr.B: Hérode avait auparavant fait arrêter Jean, l’avait fait enchaîner et jeter en prison. Il l’avait fait à cause d’Hérodiade, qui avait été la femme de son frère Philippe. \v 4 Jean, en effet, ne cessait de dire à Hérode : « La Loi ne te permet pas de l’avoir pour femme. »
fr.R: Quelque temps auparavant, Hérode avait arrêté Jean. Il l’avait attaché et mis en prison. Hérode avait fait cela à cause d’Hérodiade. Elle avait été la femme de Philippe, le frère d’Hérode, mais Hérode l’avait prise pour femme. \v 4 Jean répétait à Hérode : « La Loi de Dieu dit que tu n’as pas le droit de l’épouser ! »

sw.L: Kwa maana Herode, alipokwisha kumkamata Yohana, alikuwa amemfunga na kumweka gerezani kwa sababu ya Herodia, mke wa Filipo ndugu yake; \v 4 kwa maana Yohana alikuwa akimwambia, "Si halali wewe kuwa naye."
sw.B: Herode alikuwa amemkamata Yohana hapo awali, akamfunga minyororo na kumfungia gerezani. Alifanya hivyo kwa sababu ya Herodia, aliyekuwa mke wa Filipo ndugu yake. \v 4 Yohana alikuwa amemwambia Herode tena na tena, "Sheria haikuruhusu kuwa naye."
sw.R: Muda fulani kabla ya hapo, Herode alikuwa amemkamata Yohana. Alimfunga, akamtia gerezani. Herode alifanya hivyo kwa sababu ya Herodia. Herodia alikuwa mke wa Filipo, ndugu yake Herode, lakini Herode alikuwa amemchukua awe mke wake mwenyewe. \v 4 Yohana aliendelea kumwambia Herode, "Sheria ya Mungu inasema hupaswi kumwoa!"

vi.L: Vì Hê-rốt đã bắt Giăng, trói ông và bỏ vào ngục vì cớ Hê-rô-đia, vợ của Phi-líp, anh em mình; \v 4 vì Giăng đã nói với ông ta: "Vua không được phép lấy bà ấy."
vi.B: Trước đó, Hê-rốt đã bắt Giăng, xiềng ông lại và bỏ vào ngục. Ông ta làm vậy vì Hê-rô-đia, vợ của Phi-líp, anh em mình. \v 4 Giăng đã nhiều lần nói với Hê-rốt: "Luật pháp không cho phép vua lấy bà ấy."
vi.R: Trước đó ít lâu, Hê-rốt đã bắt Giăng. Ông ta trói Giăng lại và bỏ vào ngục. Hê-rốt làm vậy là vì Hê-rô-đia. Bà vốn là vợ của Phi-líp, anh em của Hê-rốt, nhưng Hê-rốt đã cưới bà. \v 4 Giăng cứ nói đi nói lại với Hê-rốt: "Luật pháp của Đức Chúa Trời cấm vua cưới bà ấy!"

decisions.choice: for: the story goes back to tell how John died
alternatives: the events follow Herod's words in time
decisions.reason: Matthew explains Herod's words (14:1-2) with a flashback that runs to 14:12. John's arrest was mentioned at 4:12 and his imprisonment at 11:2.

decisions.choice: Philip: the name Matthew gives Herodias's first husband, a half-brother of Antipas
alternatives: Philip the tetrarch, ruler of the lands northeast of the lake (Luke 3:1)
decisions.reason: The Jewish historian Josephus says Herodias was first married to a son of Herod the Great whom he calls Herod, and that Philip the tetrarch later married her daughter. Several sons of Herod the Great bore the family name Herod, so the first husband may also have been called Philip; Matthew follows Mark 6:17. The two accounts may name the same man differently, or one may be mistaken.

decisions.choice: the wife of Philip his brother, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the wife of his brother, without the name, in a few manuscripts
decisions.reason: A few witnesses, including Codex Bezae and some Latin manuscripts, leave out the name Philip. The sense is the same: she was his brother's wife. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: not lawful to have her: the law forbade marrying a brother's wife while the brother lived
decisions.reason: Leviticus 18:16 and 20:21 forbid a man to take his brother's wife. Herodias had left her husband, who was still alive, to marry Antipas. The verb tense says John said it more than once.

decisions.choice: had earlier (B); some time before this (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable mark the flashback plainly instead of beginning with "for".

decisions.choice: had taken her as his own wife; God's law says you must not marry her
alternatives: it is not lawful for you to have her
decisions.reason: Readable says what "have her" meant and whose law forbade it.

decisions.choice: "vua" for "you" in John's words
decisions.reason: As in Mark 6:18: a prophet rebuking a ruler addresses him by title, plainly and without the flattery of "bệ hạ".

source.text: καὶ θέλων αὐτὸν ἀποκτεῖναι ἐφοβήθη τὸν ὄχλον, ὅτι ὡς προφήτην αὐτὸν εἶχον.

records.literal_gloss: And wanting him to kill he feared the crowd, because as a prophet him they were holding.

en.L: And though he wanted to kill him, he feared the crowd, because they held him [to be] a prophet.
en.B: He would have liked to put John to death, but he was afraid of the crowds, who looked on John as a prophet.
en.R: Herod wanted to kill John. But he was afraid of the people, because they thought John was a prophet from God.

es.L: Y aunque quería matarlo, temió a la multitud, porque lo consideraban profeta.
es.B: Le habría gustado matar a Juan, pero tenía miedo de la gente, que veía en Juan a un profeta.
es.R: Herodes quería matar a Juan. Pero tenía miedo de la gente, porque pensaban que Juan era un profeta enviado por Dios.

fr.L: Et tout en voulant le tuer, il craignit la foule, parce qu’ils le tenaient pour un prophète.
fr.B: Il aurait voulu faire mourir Jean, mais il avait peur des foules, qui considéraient Jean comme un prophète.
fr.R: Hérode voulait tuer Jean. Mais il avait peur des gens, parce qu’ils pensaient que Jean était un prophète envoyé par Dieu.

sw.L: Na ingawa alitaka kumuua, aliuogopa umati, kwa sababu walimhesabu kuwa nabii.
sw.B: Alipenda kumuua Yohana, lakini aliogopa umati wa watu, ambao walimtambua Yohana kuwa nabii.
sw.R: Herode alitaka kumuua Yohana. Lakini aliwaogopa watu, kwa sababu waliamini Yohana alikuwa nabii aliyetumwa na Mungu.

vi.L: Và dù muốn giết ông, ông ta sợ dân chúng, vì họ xem ông là một nhà tiên tri.
vi.B: Hê-rốt muốn giết Giăng, nhưng ông ta sợ dân chúng, vì họ xem Giăng là một nhà tiên tri.
vi.R: Hê-rốt muốn giết Giăng. Nhưng ông ta sợ dân chúng, vì họ tin rằng Giăng là một nhà tiên tri Đức Chúa Trời sai đến.

decisions.choice: and wanting: though he wanted
decisions.reason: The participle sets Herod's wish against his fear: he wanted John dead, but fear of the people held him back.

decisions.choice: they held him as a prophet: the people believed God had sent John
alternatives: they thought him a teacher only
decisions.reason: Crowds went out to John at the Jordan (3:5), and Jesus himself called him a prophet and more (11:9). Matthew says the same of the crowds' view of John in 21:26.

decisions.choice: John
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name John so that "him" is not taken for Herod or Jesus.

source.text: γενεσίοις δὲ γενομένοις τοῦ Ἡρῴδου ὠρχήσατο ἡ θυγάτηρ τῆς Ἡρῳδιάδος ἐν τῷ μέσῳ καὶ ἤρεσεν τῷ Ἡρῴδῃ, ὅθεν μετὰ ὅρκου ὡμολόγησεν αὐτῇ δοῦναι ὃ ἐὰν αἰτήσηται.

records.literal_gloss: Birthday now having come of Herod danced the daughter of Herodias in the midst and pleased Herod, \v 7 whereupon with an oath he promised to her to give whatever she might ask.

en.L: But when Herod's birthday came, the daughter of Herodias danced in the middle [of the guests] and pleased Herod, \v 7 so that he promised with an oath to give her whatever she might ask.
en.B: When Herod's birthday was being celebrated, Herodias's daughter danced in front of everyone. Herod was so delighted with her \v 7 that he swore to give her anything she asked for.
en.R: Then came Herod's birthday party. The daughter of Herodias danced in front of Herod and his guests. Herod liked her dancing very much. \v 7 So he made a promise and swore an oath to God. He said he would give her anything she asked for.

es.L: Y cuando llegó el cumpleaños de Herodes, bailó la hija de Herodías en medio [de los invitados] y le gustó a Herodes, \v 7 de modo que con juramento se comprometió a darle cualquier cosa que pidiera.
es.B: En la fiesta de cumpleaños de Herodes, la hija de Herodías bailó delante de todos. Herodes quedó tan encantado con ella \v 7 que juró darle cualquier cosa que le pidiera.
es.R: Entonces llegó la fiesta de cumpleaños de Herodes. La hija de Herodías bailó delante de Herodes y de sus invitados. A Herodes le gustó mucho su baile. \v 7 Por eso le hizo una promesa con juramento delante de Dios: le daría cualquier cosa que pidiera.

fr.L: Or, quand vint l’anniversaire d’Hérode, la fille d’Hérodiade dansa au milieu [des invités] et plut à Hérode, \v 7 si bien qu’il promit avec serment de lui donner ce qu’elle demanderait.
fr.B: Lors de la fête d’anniversaire d’Hérode, la fille d’Hérodiade dansa devant tout le monde. Hérode fut si charmé par elle \v 7 qu’il jura de lui donner tout ce qu’elle demanderait.
fr.R: Puis est arrivé l’anniversaire d’Hérode, avec une grande fête. La fille d’Hérodiade a dansé devant Hérode et ses invités. Hérode a beaucoup aimé sa danse. \v 7 Alors il lui a fait une promesse, et il a juré devant Dieu. Il a dit qu’il lui donnerait tout ce qu’elle voudrait.

sw.L: Lakini sherehe ya siku ya kuzaliwa Herode ilipofanyika, binti wa Herodia alicheza katikati [ya wageni], na Herode akapendezwa naye, \v 7 kwa hiyo kwa kiapo aliahidi kumpa chochote ambacho angeomba.
sw.B: Siku ya sherehe ya kuzaliwa kwa Herode, binti wa Herodia alicheza mbele ya wote. Herode alifurahishwa naye sana \v 7 hata akaapa kumpa kitu chochote atakachoomba.
sw.R: Kisha ikafika sherehe ya siku ya kuzaliwa ya Herode. Binti wa Herodia alicheza mbele ya Herode na wageni wake. Herode alipenda sana uchezaji wake. \v 7 Basi akatoa ahadi, akaapa kwa jina la Mungu. Alisema atampa kitu chochote atakachoomba.

vi.L: Nhưng khi đến ngày sinh nhật của Hê-rốt, con gái của Hê-rô-đia nhảy múa ở giữa [các khách] và làm vui lòng Hê-rốt, \v 7 nên ông ta thề hứa sẽ cho cô bất cứ điều gì cô xin.
vi.B: Khi người ta mừng sinh nhật Hê-rốt, con gái của Hê-rô-đia nhảy múa trước mặt mọi người. Hê-rốt hài lòng đến nỗi \v 7 ông ta thề sẽ cho cô bất cứ điều gì cô xin.
vi.R: Rồi đến ngày tiệc sinh nhật của Hê-rốt. Con gái của Hê-rô-đia nhảy múa trước mặt Hê-rốt và các khách mời. Hê-rốt rất thích điệu múa của cô. \v 7 Vì vậy, ông ta hứa và thề trước Đức Chúa Trời. Ông ta nói sẽ cho cô bất cứ điều gì cô xin.

decisions.choice: the daughter of Herodias: her daughter by her first marriage, not named here
decisions.reason: Josephus names Herodias's daughter Salome. Matthew does not name her, and calls her a girl (14:11).

decisions.choice: birthday: the feast for Herod's birthday
alternatives: the anniversary of his coming to power
decisions.reason: The word means a birthday celebration. Mark 6:21 says Herod gave a banquet for his officials and the leading men of Galilee.

decisions.choice: with an oath: he swore by God to keep his promise
decisions.reason: An oath called on God as witness, and breaking it was a serious matter (5:33). Jesus had warned against swearing at all (5:34-37).

decisions.choice: whereupon: so that, as a result
decisions.reason: The word gives the result of Herod's delight in the dance.

decisions.choice: in the middle [of the guests]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the guests implied by the banquet (14:9).

decisions.choice: swore an oath to God
decisions.reason: Readable says to whom an oath was sworn.

decisions.choice: "ở giữa [các khách]" (L)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese, like English, needs to say whom she danced among; Literal brackets it.

source.text: ἡ δὲ προβιβασθεῖσα ὑπὸ τῆς μητρὸς αὐτῆς· Δός μοι, φησίν, ὧδε ἐπὶ πίνακι τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἰωάννου τοῦ βαπτιστοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And she having been urged on by the mother of her, Give me, she says, here on a platter the head of John the Baptist.

en.L: And she, having been prompted by her mother, says, "Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptist."
en.B: Her mother told her what to say, and she answered, "Give me the head of John the Baptist on a platter, right here."
en.R: The girl's mother told her what to ask for. So the girl said to Herod, "Give me the head of John the Baptist on a big plate. Give it to me right here."

es.L: Y ella, inducida por su madre: «Dame —dice— aquí, en una bandeja, la cabeza de Juan el Bautista».
es.B: Su madre le dijo lo que tenía que decir, y ella respondió: «Dame la cabeza de Juan el Bautista en una bandeja, aquí mismo».
es.R: La madre de la muchacha le dijo qué debía pedir. Entonces la muchacha le dijo a Herodes: «Dame la cabeza de Juan el Bautista en una bandeja grande. Dámela aquí mismo».

fr.L: Et elle, poussée par sa mère : « Donne-moi, dit-elle, ici, sur un plat, la tête de Jean le Baptiste. »
fr.B: Sa mère lui dicta ce qu’elle devait dire, et elle répondit : « Donne-moi sur un plat la tête de Jean le Baptiste, ici même. »
fr.R: La mère de la jeune fille lui a dit ce qu’elle devait demander. Alors la jeune fille a dit à Hérode : « Donne-moi la tête de Jean le Baptiste sur un grand plat. Donne-la-moi tout de suite, ici. »

sw.L: Naye, akiwa amechochewa na mama yake, "Nipe," anasema, "hapa katika sinia kichwa cha Yohana Mbatizaji."
sw.B: Mama yake alimwambia la kusema, naye akajibu, "Nipe kichwa cha Yohana Mbatizaji juu ya sinia, papa hapa."
sw.R: Mama yake msichana alimwambia aombe nini. Basi msichana akamwambia Herode, "Nipe kichwa cha Yohana Mbatizaji katika sinia kubwa. Nipe hapa hapa sasa hivi."

vi.L: Và cô, bị mẹ mình xui giục, nói: "Xin ban cho con cái đầu của Giăng Báp-tít, đặt trên một cái mâm, ngay tại đây."
vi.B: Được mẹ dặn trước, cô thưa: "Xin bệ hạ ban cho con cái đầu của Giăng Báp-tít, đặt trên mâm, ngay tại đây."
vi.R: Mẹ của cô gái đã dặn cô phải xin điều gì. Vì vậy, cô gái nói với Hê-rốt: "Xin bệ hạ cho con cái đầu của Giăng Báp-tít, đặt trên một cái mâm lớn. Xin cho con ngay tại đây!"

decisions.choice: having been prompted: urged on beforehand by her mother
alternatives: led forward by her mother onto the floor
decisions.reason: The verb means to push forward or put up to something. Mark 6:24 tells how the girl went out and asked her mother what to request.

decisions.choice: platter: a flat dish for serving food
decisions.reason: The word means a wide plate or dish, such as the dishes used at Herod's feast.

decisions.choice: here: at once, at the feast
decisions.reason: She wants the deed done now, before Herod can change his mind.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: the head of John the Baptist on a platter, right here
alternatives: here on a platter the head of John the Baptist
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the request first and the place last, which reads more naturally.

decisions.choice: una bandeja
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a flat dish for serving food (meaning decision m2). "Bandeja" is a large dish for carrying food to the table; "plato" suggests an ordinary plate.

decisions.choice: Dame —dice— aquí (L); respondió (B); le dijo (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek puts "she says" inside the request, in the present. Spanish can do the same with dashes, so Literal keeps both; Balanced and Readable tell it in the past, as the English does.

decisions.choice: sinia
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a flat dish for serving food (meaning decision m2). "Sinia" is the large tray on which food is carried in; "sahani" is an ordinary plate.

decisions.choice: "Nipe," anasema, "hapa ..." (L); akajibu (B); akamwambia (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek puts "she says" inside the request, in the present. Swahili can do the same, so Literal keeps both; Balanced and Readable tell it in the narrative past.

decisions.choice: "xin" and "con" for the girl; "bệ hạ" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 6:25: a girl asking a favour of the ruler speaks humbly as "con" and uses the court word "bệ hạ"; Literal leaves the address out, as the Greek does. "Nói" has no "đã" at Literal, where Matthew uses the present.

source.text: καὶ λυπηθεὶς ὁ βασιλεὺς διὰ τοὺς ὅρκους καὶ τοὺς συνανακειμένους ἐκέλευσεν δοθῆναι, καὶ πέμψας ἀπεκεφάλισεν τὸν Ἰωάννην ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ·

records.literal_gloss: And having been grieved the king because of the oaths and those reclining with [him] he commanded [it] to be given, \v 10 and having sent he beheaded John in the prison;

en.L: And the king was grieved, [but] because of the oaths and those reclining [at table] with [him], he commanded [it] to be given, \v 10 and he sent and beheaded John in the prison.
en.B: This grieved the king. Yet because of his oaths, and because of the guests at his table, he gave orders for her request to be granted. \v 10 He sent word to the prison, and there John was beheaded.
en.R: The king was very sad. But he had sworn an oath, and his dinner guests had heard him. So he ordered his men to give the girl what she asked for. \v 10 He sent them to the prison, and they cut off John's head there.

es.L: Y entristecido el rey, por los juramentos y por los que estaban recostados [a la mesa] con [él], ordenó que se [le] diera, \v 10 y envió a decapitar a Juan en la cárcel.
es.B: Esto entristeció al rey. Pero a causa de sus juramentos, y por los invitados que estaban a su mesa, ordenó que se cumpliera lo que ella pedía. \v 10 Envió órdenes a la cárcel, y allí decapitaron a Juan.
es.R: El rey se puso muy triste. Pero había hecho un juramento, y sus invitados lo habían oído. Por eso ordenó a sus hombres que le dieran a la muchacha lo que había pedido. \v 10 Los mandó a la cárcel, y allí le cortaron la cabeza a Juan.

fr.L: Et le roi fut attristé, [mais] à cause des serments et de ceux qui étaient à table avec [lui], il ordonna qu’on la lui donne, \v 10 et il envoya décapiter Jean dans la prison.
fr.B: Le roi en fut attristé. Pourtant, à cause de ses serments et des convives qui étaient à sa table, il ordonna de la lui accorder. \v 10 Il envoya un ordre à la prison, et là Jean fut décapité.
fr.R: Le roi était très triste. Mais il avait fait un serment, et ses invités l’avaient entendu. Alors il a ordonné à ses hommes de donner à la jeune fille ce qu’elle demandait. \v 10 Il les a envoyés à la prison, et là, ils ont coupé la tête de Jean.

sw.L: Na mfalme akahuzunika; [lakini] kwa sababu ya viapo na wale walioegemea [mezani] pamoja [naye], akaagiza apatiwe [alichoomba], \v 10 akatuma watu, akamkata Yohana kichwa ndani ya gereza.
sw.B: Jambo hili lilimhuzunisha mfalme. Hata hivyo, kwa sababu ya viapo vyake na kwa sababu ya wageni waliokuwa mezani pamoja naye, aliagiza ombi lake litimizwe. \v 10 Alituma ujumbe gerezani, na huko Yohana akakatwa kichwa.
sw.R: Mfalme alihuzunika sana. Lakini alikuwa ameapa, na wageni wake walikuwa wamemsikia. Kwa hiyo akawaamuru watu wake wampe msichana kile alichoomba. \v 10 Akawatuma gerezani, nao wakamkata Yohana kichwa huko.

vi.L: Và vua buồn rầu, [nhưng] vì những lời thề và vì những người cùng ngồi dự tiệc, ông ta truyền lệnh cho [cô], \v 10 và sai người chém đầu Giăng trong ngục.
vi.B: Vua rất buồn. Nhưng vì đã thề, và vì các khách dự tiệc, ông ta ra lệnh ban cho cô điều cô xin. \v 10 Ông ta sai người vào ngục chém đầu Giăng.
vi.R: Vua rất buồn. Nhưng ông ta đã thề, và các khách dự tiệc đều đã nghe. Vì vậy, ông ta ra lệnh cho người của mình làm theo điều cô gái xin. \v 10 Ông ta sai họ đến nhà ngục, và họ chém đầu Giăng ở đó.

decisions.choice: the king: Herod, called king loosely
decisions.reason: Antipas was a tetrarch (14:1), not a king, but people called him king (Mark 6:14). Years later he asked Rome for the title and lost his rule instead.

decisions.choice: grieved: sorry, distressed
decisions.reason: Herod regrets what he must do: he wanted John dead (14:5) but feared the people, and now he is trapped by his own oath.

decisions.choice: the oaths and those reclining with him: the oaths sworn before his dinner guests
alternatives: two separate reasons with no link
decisions.reason: Guests reclined on couches at a feast. To break an oath sworn in front of them would shame Herod. The plural "oaths" may mean he swore more than once.

decisions.choice: having sent, he beheaded John: he had John beheaded by others
alternatives: Herod did it with his own hand
decisions.reason: As often, the one who gives the order is said to do the deed. Mark 6:27 names an executioner.

decisions.choice: sent word to the prison (B); sent them to the prison (R)
alternatives: having sent, he beheaded John in the prison
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where the order went and who carried it out.

decisions.choice: he had sworn an oath, and his dinner guests had heard him
alternatives: because of the oaths and the guests
decisions.reason: Readable spells out why the oath and the guests together held Herod to his word.

decisions.choice: "il envoya décapiter Jean"
decisions.reason: French "envoyer" followed by an infinitive says in two words that Herod had John beheaded by others (m4); copying the two Greek verbs would make Herod the executioner.

decisions.choice: "vua" for Herod
decisions.reason: Matthew calls the tetrarch "king" loosely here (meaning decision), and Vietnamese keeps the word, as Mark 6:26 does.

decisions.choice: "sai người chém đầu" (L)
decisions.reason: He had John beheaded by others (meaning decision); Vietnamese "sai người" says it without a bracket.

source.text: καὶ ἠνέχθη ἡ κεφαλὴ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ πίνακι καὶ ἐδόθη τῷ κορασίῳ, καὶ ἤνεγκεν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτῆς.

records.literal_gloss: And was brought the head of him on a platter and was given to the girl, and she brought [it] to the mother of her.

en.L: And his head was brought on a platter and given to the girl, and she brought [it] to her mother.
en.B: Someone carried the head in on a platter and gave it to the girl, and she in turn brought it to her mother.
en.R: A man brought John's head on a plate and gave it to the girl. Then the girl took it to her mother.

es.L: Y su cabeza fue traída sobre una bandeja y entregada a la muchacha, y ella [la] llevó a su madre.
es.B: Alguien trajo la cabeza en una bandeja y se la dio a la muchacha, y ella a su vez se la llevó a su madre.
es.R: Un hombre trajo la cabeza de Juan en una bandeja y se la dio a la muchacha. Luego la muchacha se la llevó a su madre.

fr.L: Et sa tête fut apportée sur un plat et donnée à la jeune fille, et elle [l’]apporta à sa mère.
fr.B: On apporta la tête sur un plat et on la donna à la jeune fille, qui la porta à son tour à sa mère.
fr.R: Un homme a apporté la tête de Jean sur un plat et il l’a donnée à la jeune fille. Ensuite, la jeune fille l’a portée à sa mère.

sw.L: Na kichwa chake kililetwa juu ya sinia na kupewa msichana, naye [akakipeleka] kwa mama yake.
sw.B: Mtu mmoja alikileta kichwa katika sinia, akampa msichana, naye akampelekea mama yake.
sw.R: Mtu mmoja alileta kichwa cha Yohana katika sinia, akampa msichana. Kisha msichana akakipeleka kwa mama yake.

vi.L: Và đầu ông được đem đến trên một cái mâm và trao cho cô gái, và cô đem đến cho mẹ mình.
vi.B: Người ta bưng đầu Giăng trên một cái mâm vào trao cho cô gái, và cô đem đến cho mẹ mình.
vi.R: Một người lính mang đầu Giăng trên một cái mâm đến và đưa cho cô gái. Rồi cô gái đem cái đầu ấy đến cho mẹ mình.

decisions.choice: girl: a young girl
decisions.reason: The word is a diminutive used of a girl not yet grown, as of Jairus's daughter (9:24-25).

decisions.choice: she brought it to her mother: the request was the mother's from the start
decisions.reason: The story ends with Herodias, who wanted John silenced (14:3-4, 8).

decisions.choice: someone carried (B); a man brought (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the passive verb a subject; Matthew does not say who it was.

source.text: καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἦραν τὸ πτῶμα καὶ ἔθαψαν αὐτόν, καὶ ἐλθόντες ἀπήγγειλαν τῷ Ἰησοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And having come the disciples of him took the corpse and buried it, and having come they told Jesus.

en.L: And his disciples came and took the body and buried it, and they went and told Jesus.
en.B: Then John's disciples came for his body and buried it, and they went to tell Jesus what had happened.
en.R: John's followers came and took his body away, and they buried it. Then they went and told Jesus what had happened.

es.L: Y acercándose sus discípulos, tomaron el cadáver y lo sepultaron, y fueron y [se lo] anunciaron a Jesús.
es.B: Entonces los discípulos de Juan vinieron a recoger su cuerpo y lo sepultaron, y fueron a contarle a Jesús lo que había pasado.
es.R: Los seguidores de Juan vinieron y se llevaron su cuerpo, y lo enterraron. Luego fueron y le contaron a Jesús lo que había pasado.

fr.L: Et ses disciples vinrent, emportèrent le corps et l’ensevelirent, et ils allèrent l’annoncer à Jésus.
fr.B: Les disciples de Jean vinrent alors chercher son corps et l’ensevelirent, puis ils allèrent raconter à Jésus ce qui s’était passé.
fr.R: Les disciples de Jean sont venus emporter son corps, et ils l’ont enterré. Ensuite, ils sont allés raconter à Jésus ce qui s’était passé.

sw.L: Na wanafunzi wake wakaja, wakaichukua maiti, wakaizika, na walipofika wakampa Yesu habari.
sw.B: Kisha wanafunzi wa Yohana walikuja kuuchukua mwili wake, wakauzika, wakaenda kumweleza Yesu yaliyotokea.
sw.R: Wanafunzi wa Yohana walikuja, wakauchukua mwili wake, wakauzika. Kisha wakaenda kumwambia Yesu mambo yaliyotokea.

vi.L: Và các môn đồ của ông đến lấy thi hài và chôn cất, rồi đi báo tin cho Đức Giê-xu.
vi.B: Các môn đồ của Giăng đến lấy thi hài ông đem đi chôn, rồi đi báo tin cho Đức Giê-xu.
vi.R: Các môn đồ của Giăng đến mang xác ông đi và chôn cất. Rồi họ đi kể cho Đức Giê-xu nghe chuyện đã xảy ra.

decisions.choice: his disciples: John's disciples
decisions.reason: John had disciples of his own (9:14; 11:2). They give their teacher the burial owed to the dead.

decisions.choice: body: a dead body, a corpse
decisions.reason: The word is used only of the dead.

decisions.choice: they told Jesus: John's death points ahead to Jesus's own
alternatives: a report with no further meaning
decisions.reason: John went before Jesus in his preaching (3:2; 4:17), in being handed over (4:12; 17:22), and now in death. Jesus later says that as they did to John, so the Son of Man will suffer (17:12).

decisions.choice: John's; what had happened
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name whose disciples these were and say what they reported.

source.text: Ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀνεχώρησεν ἐκεῖθεν ἐν πλοίῳ εἰς ἔρημον τόπον κατ’ ἰδίαν· καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ ὄχλοι ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ πεζῇ ἀπὸ τῶν πόλεων.

records.literal_gloss: Having heard now Jesus withdrew from there in a boat to a deserted place by himself; and having heard the crowds followed him on foot from the towns.

en.L: Now when Jesus heard [it], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} withdrew from there in a boat to a deserted place by {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}; and when the crowds heard [of it], they followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on foot from the towns.
en.B: When Jesus heard the news, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got into a boat and went off to a deserted place to be alone. But the crowds found out, and they came after {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on foot from the towns.
en.R: Jesus heard what had happened to John. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left in a boat and went to a quiet place where no one lived. He wanted to be alone. But the crowds heard where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was going. They left their towns and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, walking along the shore.

es.L: Al oír [esto], Jesús se retiró de allí en una barca a un lugar desierto, a solas; y al oír[lo] las multitudes, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguieron a pie desde las ciudades.
es.B: Cuando Jesús se enteró de la noticia, subió a una barca y se fue a un lugar apartado para estar a solas. Pero las multitudes se enteraron y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguieron a pie desde los pueblos.
es.R: Jesús oyó lo que le había pasado a Juan. Por eso se fue en una barca a un lugar tranquilo donde no vivía nadie. Quería estar solo. Pero las multitudes oyeron adónde iba. Dejaron sus pueblos y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguieron caminando por la orilla.

fr.L: Or Jésus, l’ayant appris, se retira de là en barque vers un lieu désert, à l’écart ; et les foules, l’ayant appris, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivirent à pied depuis les villes.
fr.B: Quand Jésus apprit la nouvelle, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} monta dans une barque et s’en alla dans un endroit isolé pour être seul. Mais les foules l’apprirent et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivirent à pied depuis les villes.
fr.R: Jésus a appris ce qui était arrivé à Jean. Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est parti en bateau vers un endroit tranquille où personne n’habitait. Il voulait être seul. Mais les foules ont appris où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} allait. Elles ont quitté leurs villes et {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont suivi à pied en longeant le bord du lac.

sw.L: Lakini Yesu aliposikia [hayo], alijitenga kutoka huko kwa mashua akaenda mahali pasipo na makazi, peke {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}; na umati wa watu uliposikia [habari], ukamfuata kwa miguu kutoka katika miji.
sw.B: Yesu aliposikia habari hizo, alipanda mashua, akaenda mahali palipo faragha ili awe peke {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Lakini umati ulipata habari, ukamfuata kwa miguu kutoka mijini.
sw.R: Yesu alisikia mambo yaliyompata Yohana. Basi akaondoka kwa mashua, akaenda mahali patulivu ambapo hapakuwa na watu. Alitaka kuwa peke {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Lakini umati wa watu ulisikia alikokuwa akienda. Wakaacha miji yao, wakamfuata, wakitembea kando ya ziwa.

vi.L: Nghe [vậy], Đức Giê-xu rời khỏi đó, đi thuyền đến một nơi hoang vắng, riêng một mình; và khi đoàn dân nghe [tin], họ từ các thành đi bộ theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Nghe tin ấy, Đức Giê-xu xuống thuyền rời khỏi đó, đến một nơi hoang vắng để ở một mình. Nhưng đoàn dân hay được, và từ các thành, họ đi bộ theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Khi nghe chuyện đã xảy ra cho Giăng, Đức Giê-xu lên thuyền rời khỏi nơi đó. Ngài đến một nơi yên tĩnh, không có ai ở. Ngài muốn ở một mình. Nhưng dân chúng nghe biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi đâu. Họ rời các thị trấn của mình và đi bộ dọc theo bờ hồ mà theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

decisions.choice: having heard: Jesus heard of John's death, just reported to him
alternatives: he heard what Herod was saying about him (14:1-2)
decisions.reason: The verse follows the report of John's disciples (14:12), so the news of John's death is the nearest meaning. Because 14:3-12 looks back in time, some link it to Herod's words in 14:1-2 instead. Either way, Herod's attention is now on Jesus.

decisions.choice: withdrew: went away, as Matthew says when danger is near
decisions.reason: Matthew uses the verb when Jesus moves away from a threat (2:14, 22; 4:12; 12:15).

decisions.choice: a deserted place: a lonely place with no village
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the wilderness. It was open country without towns, which is why the disciples worry about food (14:15).

decisions.choice: what had happened to John; walking along the shore
decisions.reason: Readable says what Jesus heard, as the meaning note explains, and that the crowds went by land around the lake while he went by boat. Matthew does not describe their route.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans on separate pronouns only: lo (him); none for "he" or "by himself" (a solas)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish leaves the subject pronoun out and says "by himself" with "a solas", so there is nothing separate to capitalise. The setting therefore covers fewer words than in English; the same through the passage.

decisions.choice: "à l’écart" (L); "pour être seul" (B)
decisions.reason: English Literal says "by himself" and carries a pronoun span; French "à l’écart" says the same without a pronoun, so Literal has no span there.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans on free pronouns only: peke yake (by himself); none on akamfuata (followed him)
decisions.reason: Swahili carries "he" and "him" in the verb, where a prefix cannot take a capital, so the setting covers only free pronouns and possessives, as in John and Mark. Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English through the passage.

decisions.choice: "riêng một mình" (L); "để ở một mình" (B); "muốn ở một mình" (R), with no setting
decisions.reason: Vietnamese says "by himself" with "một mình", which is not a pronoun, so the English deity_pronoun span on "himself" has no counterpart.

source.text: καὶ ἐξελθὼν εἶδεν πολὺν ὄχλον, καὶ ἐσπλαγχνίσθη ἐπ’ αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν τοὺς ἀρρώστους αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And having gone out he saw a great crowd, and he was moved with compassion toward them and healed the sick of them.

en.L: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went ashore, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw a great crowd, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had compassion on them and healed their sick.
en.B: As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stepped ashore, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw a large crowd. He felt deep pity for them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed those among them who were sick.
en.R: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got out of the boat, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw a large crowd. He felt sorry for them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed the people who were sick.

es.L: Y al desembarcar vio una gran multitud, y se compadeció de ellos y sanó a sus enfermos.
es.B: Al bajar a tierra vio una gran multitud. Sintió profunda compasión por ellos, y sanó a los que estaban enfermos.
es.R: Cuando bajó de la barca, vio mucha gente. Sintió lástima por ellos y sanó a los enfermos.

fr.L: Et en débarquant, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vit une grande foule, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fut ému de compassion pour eux et guérit leurs malades.
fr.B: Lorsqu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} débarqua, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vit une grande foule. Il fut pris de pitié pour eux, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} guérit ceux d’entre eux qui étaient malades.
fr.R: Quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est descendu du bateau, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a vu une grande foule. Il a eu pitié de ces gens, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a guéri les malades.

sw.L: Na alipotoka [mashuani], akaona umati mkubwa, akaguswa moyoni kwa huruma kwa ajili yao, akawaponya wagonjwa wao.
sw.B: Alipotoka mashuani, aliona umati mkubwa. Akawaonea huruma kubwa, akawaponya wale waliokuwa wagonjwa miongoni mwao.
sw.R: Alipotoka mashuani, aliona umati mkubwa wa watu. Akawaonea huruma, akawaponya watu waliokuwa wagonjwa.

vi.L: Và khi ra [khỏi thuyền], {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thấy một đoàn dân đông, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} động lòng thương xót họ và chữa lành những người bệnh của họ.
vi.B: Khi lên bờ, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thấy một đoàn dân rất đông. Ngài thương xót họ sâu xa và chữa lành những người bệnh trong vòng họ.
vi.R: Khi ra khỏi thuyền, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thấy rất đông người. Ngài thương họ, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chữa lành những người bệnh.

decisions.choice: having gone out: having come out of the boat
alternatives: having come out of the deserted place to meet them
decisions.reason: Jesus came by boat (14:13), and the crowd had gone ahead on foot. He gets out and finds them already there.

decisions.choice: had compassion: was moved deep within
decisions.reason: As in 9:36, the verb speaks of strong feeling. Jesus had sought to be alone, but he does not send the crowd away.

decisions.choice: went ashore (L); stepped ashore (B); got out of the boat (R)
decisions.reason: Every level says what Jesus went out of, so that the reader does not picture him leaving the lonely place.

decisions.choice: "động lòng thương xót" (L); "thương xót ... sâu xa" (B); "thương" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 6:34 and 9:36 in the Vietnamese Matthew: moved deep within (meaning decision).

source.text: ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης προσῆλθον αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ λέγοντες· Ἔρημός ἐστιν ὁ τόπος καὶ ἡ ὥρα ἤδη παρῆλθεν· ἀπόλυσον τοὺς ὄχλους, ἵνα ἀπελθόντες εἰς τὰς κώμας ἀγοράσωσιν ἑαυτοῖς βρώματα.

records.literal_gloss: Evening now having come came to him the disciples saying, Deserted is the place and the hour already has passed; dismiss the crowds, that having gone into the villages they may buy for themselves food.

en.L: Now when evening came, the disciples came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "The place is deserted, and the hour has already passed. Send the crowds away, so that they may go into the villages and buy food for themselves."
en.B: When evening came, the disciples went to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said, "There is nothing out here, and the day is nearly over. Let the crowds go now, so they can find food to buy in the villages."
en.R: Late in the afternoon, the followers came to Jesus. They said, "No one lives out here, and it is getting late. Send the people away. Then they can go to the villages and buy some food for themselves."

es.L: Llegada la tarde, se {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} acercaron los discípulos, diciendo: «Despoblado es el lugar, y la hora ya pasó; despide a las multitudes, para que, yendo a las aldeas, se compren comida».
es.B: Al atardecer, los discípulos se acercaron a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «Aquí no hay nada, y el día ya se acaba. Deja ir ya a la gente, para que puedan comprar comida en las aldeas».
es.R: Al final de la tarde, los seguidores se acercaron a Jesús. Le dijeron: «Aquí no vive nadie, y ya se está haciendo tarde. Despide a la gente. Así podrán ir a las aldeas y comprarse algo de comer».

fr.L: Le soir venu, les disciples vinrent à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, disant : « Le lieu est désert, et l’heure est déjà passée ; renvoie les foules, afin qu’elles aillent dans les villages s’acheter de la nourriture. »
fr.B: Le soir venu, les disciples s’approchèrent de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et dirent : « Il n’y a rien ici, et la journée est presque finie. Laisse partir les foules maintenant, pour qu’elles aillent dans les villages acheter de quoi manger. »
fr.R: En fin d’après-midi, les disciples sont venus trouver Jésus. Ils ont dit : « Personne n’habite ici, et il se fait tard. Renvoie les gens. Ils pourront aller dans les villages et s’acheter quelque chose à manger. »

sw.L: Jioni ilipofika, wanafunzi walimjia wakisema, "Ni mahali pasipo na watu hapa, na saa imeshapita. Waache umati waende, ili wakiingia vijijini wajinunulie chakula."
sw.B: Ilipofika jioni, wanafunzi walimwendea wakamwambia, "Hakuna kitu huku nje, na mchana unakaribia kwisha. Uwaruhusu watu waondoke sasa, ili wakatafute chakula cha kununua vijijini."
sw.R: Alasiri, wanafunzi walimwendea Yesu. Wakasema, "Hakuna watu wanaoishi huku, na sasa ni jioni. Waambie watu hawa waondoke. Waende vijijini wakajinunulie chakula."

vi.L: Khi chiều đến, các môn đồ đến gần {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và nói: "Nơi này hoang vắng, và giờ đã muộn rồi; xin Thầy giải tán đoàn dân, để họ đi vào các làng mà tự mua thức ăn."
vi.B: Chiều tối hôm ấy, các môn đồ đến thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Ở đây không có nhà cửa gì cả, mà trời đã muộn rồi. Xin Thầy cho dân chúng về, để họ vào các làng mua đồ ăn."
vi.R: Gần cuối buổi chiều, các môn đồ đến gặp Đức Giê-xu. Họ thưa: "Gần đây không có ai ở, mà trời đã muộn rồi. Xin Thầy bảo dân chúng về đi. Như thế họ có thể vào các làng mua chút gì để ăn."

decisions.choice: evening: late in the afternoon, toward sunset
decisions.reason: The word covers the late part of the day. There is still time to reach the villages and buy food. A later "evening" in 14:23 is after dark.

decisions.choice: the hour has already passed: it is late in the day
decisions.reason: Both senses fit: the day is far gone, and the people have not eaten. The disciples' point is that there is little time left.

decisions.choice: dismiss: send away, let go
decisions.reason: The disciples ask Jesus to end the gathering so the people can look after themselves.

decisions.choice: late in the afternoon; the followers
decisions.reason: Readable gives the time of day in modern terms and says what disciples are.

decisions.choice: "les disciples"
decisions.reason: French keeps "disciples" at every level (style guide section 5), as Mark 6:35 does at Readable; it is a word young French readers meet in church and school. The same holds in 14:19-20.

decisions.choice: "xin Thầy" with the command
decisions.reason: As in Mark 6:36: disciples cannot give their teacher a bare order in Vietnamese; "xin" and the address "Thầy" make it a request. They are words of address that Vietnamese grammar requires, so Literal does not bracket them.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν ἀπελθεῖν· δότε αὐτοῖς ὑμεῖς φαγεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: But Jesus said to them, No need they have to go away; give them you to eat.

en.L: But Jesus said to them, "They have no need to go away; you give them [something] to eat."
en.B: But Jesus told them, "They do not have to go away. Give them food yourselves."
en.R: But Jesus said to them, "They do not need to leave. You feed them yourselves."

es.L: Pero Jesús les dijo: «No les hace falta irse; {{plural_you:denles|dadles}} {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} de comer».
es.B: Pero Jesús les dijo: «No tienen por qué irse. {{plural_you:Denles|Dadles}} de comer {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos».
es.R: Pero Jesús les dijo: «No hace falta que se vayan. {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}} mismos {{plural_you:denles|dadles}} de comer».

fr.L: Mais Jésus leur dit : « Ils n’ont pas besoin de s’en aller ; vous, donnez-leur à manger. »
fr.B: Mais Jésus leur dit : « Ils n’ont pas besoin de partir. Donnez-leur vous-mêmes à manger. »
fr.R: Mais Jésus leur a dit : « Ils n’ont pas besoin de partir. C’est vous qui allez leur donner à manger. »

sw.L: Lakini Yesu akawaambia, "Hawahitaji kuondoka; ninyi wapeni [kitu cha] kula."
sw.B: Lakini Yesu akawaambia, "Si lazima waondoke. Ninyi wenyewe wapeni chakula."
sw.R: Lakini Yesu akawaambia, "Hakuna haja waondoke. Ninyi wenyewe walisheni."

vi.L: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Họ không cần phải đi; chính các con hãy cho họ ăn."
vi.B: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu bảo họ: "Họ không cần phải đi đâu. Chính các con hãy cho họ ăn đi."
vi.R: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Họ không cần phải đi. Các con hãy tự cho họ ăn."

decisions.choice: you: the pronoun is stressed: you yourselves
decisions.reason: The Greek adds the pronoun for emphasis. Jesus puts the task on the disciples, who know they have almost nothing.

decisions.choice: give them to eat: perhaps an echo of Elisha feeding a hundred men
decisions.reason: Elisha told his servant to set a few loaves before a hundred men, and they ate and had some left over (2 Kings 4:42-44). Matthew does not cite the passage.

decisions.choice: yourselves
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable carry the stressed "you" with "yourselves".

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:denles|dadles}} {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the disciples, so every plural "you" and its verb is the reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain). The pronoun is kept because the Greek stresses it (meaning decision m1). The same through the passage.

decisions.choice: "chính các con" (L, B); "các con hãy tự" (R)
decisions.reason: The pronoun is stressed (meaning decision), as in Mark 6:37.

source.text: οἱ δὲ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Οὐκ ἔχομεν ὧδε εἰ μὴ πέντε ἄρτους καὶ δύο ἰχθύας.

records.literal_gloss: And they say to him, Not we have here except five loaves and two fish.

en.L: And they say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "We have nothing here except five loaves and two fish."
en.B: They said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "We have nothing here but five loaves and two fish."
en.R: They said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "All we have here are five small loaves of bread and two fish."

es.L: Y ellos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dicen: «Aquí no tenemos más que cinco panes y dos pescados».
es.B: Ellos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respondieron: «Aquí solo tenemos cinco panes y dos pescados».
es.R: Ellos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «Lo único que tenemos aquí son cinco panecillos y dos pescados».

fr.L: Et ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} disent : « Nous n’avons ici que cinq pains et deux poissons. »
fr.B: Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dirent : « Nous n’avons ici rien d’autre que cinq pains et deux poissons. »
fr.R: Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont dit : « Nous avons seulement cinq petits pains et deux poissons. »

sw.L: Nao wanamwambia, "Hapa hatuna [chochote] isipokuwa mikate mitano na samaki wawili."
sw.B: Wakamwambia, "Tulicho nacho hapa ni mikate mitano na samaki wawili tu."
sw.R: Wakamwambia, "Hapa tuna mikate midogo mitano na samaki wawili tu."

vi.L: Họ nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Ở đây chúng con chẳng có gì ngoài năm cái bánh và hai con cá."
vi.B: Họ thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Ở đây chúng con chỉ có năm cái bánh và hai con cá thôi."
vi.R: Họ thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Ở đây chúng con chỉ có năm cái bánh nhỏ và hai con cá."

decisions.choice: loaves: small flat round loaves, each about a meal for one
decisions.reason: Bread was baked in small round flat loaves. Five of them would feed a few people. John 6:9 says they were barley loaves.

decisions.choice: fish: small fish, probably dried or salted
decisions.reason: Fish from the lake were salted or dried and eaten with bread.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: small loaves of bread
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of loaves these were.

decisions.choice: "nói" with no "đã" (L)
decisions.reason: Matthew uses the present "they say"; Literal keeps it by leaving out "đã".

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Φέρετέ μοι ὧδε αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: And he said, Bring to me here them.

en.B: He told them, "Bring them over here to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.R: Jesus said, "Bring the bread and fish here to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

es.R: Jesús dijo: «{{plural_you:Tráiganme|Traedme}} aquí el pan y los pescados».

fr.B: Il leur dit : « Apportez-les ici, près de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. »
fr.R: Jésus a dit : « Apportez-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} le pain et les poissons ici. »

sw.R: Yesu akasema, "Leteni mikate na samaki hapa {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}."

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói: "Hãy đem chúng đến đây cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."
vi.B: Ngài bảo: "Hãy đem đến đây cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói: "Hãy đem bánh và cá đến đây cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."

decisions.choice: bring them to me: the little they have is put in Jesus's hands
decisions.reason: The command moves the food from the disciples to Jesus before the crowd is fed.

decisions.choice: the bread and fish
decisions.reason: Readable names what is to be brought.

source.text: καὶ κελεύσας τοὺς ὄχλους ἀνακλιθῆναι ἐπὶ τοῦ χόρτου, λαβὼν τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους καὶ τοὺς δύο ἰχθύας, ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εὐλόγησεν καὶ κλάσας ἔδωκεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς τοὺς ἄρτους οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ τοῖς ὄχλοις.

records.literal_gloss: And having commanded the crowds to recline on the grass, having taken the five loaves and the two fish, having looked up to the heaven he blessed, and having broken he gave to the disciples the loaves, and the disciples to the crowds.

en.L: And having ordered the crowds to recline on the grass, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the five loaves and the two fish, looked up to heaven, [and] blessed, and having broken [them] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave the loaves to the disciples, and the disciples [gave them] to the crowds.
en.B: He had the people sit down on the grass. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the five loaves and the two fish, raised {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes to heaven, and spoke the blessing. He broke the loaves and handed them to the disciples, and the disciples passed them to the crowds.
en.R: Jesus told the people to sit down on the grass. He took the five loaves and the two fish, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} looked up to heaven and thanked God for the food. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke the loaves into pieces and gave them to the followers. The followers gave the food to the people.

es.L: Y tras ordenar que las multitudes se recostaran sobre la hierba, tomó los cinco panes y los dos pescados, alzó la mirada al cielo [y] pronunció la bendición, y partiendo [los panes] dio los panes a los discípulos, y los discípulos [los dieron] a las multitudes.
es.B: Mandó a la gente que se sentara sobre la hierba. Luego tomó los cinco panes y los dos pescados, levantó {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mirada al cielo y pronunció la bendición. Partió los panes y se los entregó a los discípulos, y los discípulos los repartieron a la gente.
es.R: Jesús le dijo a la gente que se sentara sobre la hierba. Tomó los cinco panes y los dos pescados, miró al cielo y le dio gracias a Dios por la comida. Luego partió los panes en pedazos y se los dio a los seguidores. Los seguidores le dieron la comida a la gente.

fr.L: Et ayant ordonné aux foules de s’allonger sur l’herbe, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} prit les cinq pains et les deux poissons, leva les yeux vers le ciel et bénit, et [les] ayant rompus, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} donna les pains aux disciples, et les disciples [les donnèrent] aux foules.
fr.B: Il fit asseoir la foule sur l’herbe. Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} prit les cinq pains et les deux poissons, leva les yeux vers le ciel et prononça la bénédiction. Il rompit les pains et les donna aux disciples, et les disciples les distribuèrent aux foules.
fr.R: Jésus a dit aux gens de s’asseoir sur l’herbe. Il a pris les cinq pains et les deux poissons, puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a levé les yeux vers le ciel et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a remercié Dieu pour la nourriture. Ensuite, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a rompu les pains en morceaux et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a donnés aux disciples. Les disciples ont donné la nourriture aux gens.

sw.L: Na akiisha kuagiza umati wa watu waegemee juu ya nyasi, akachukua mikate ile mitano na samaki wale wawili, akainua macho kuelekea mbinguni, akabariki, na baada ya kuimega akawapa wanafunzi mikate, nao wanafunzi [wakawapa] umati.
sw.B: Aliwaambia watu waketi kwenye nyasi. Kisha akachukua mikate mitano na samaki wawili, akainua macho {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kuelekea mbinguni, akasema maneno ya baraka. Akaimega mikate, akawakabidhi wanafunzi, nao wanafunzi wakawagawia watu.
sw.R: Yesu aliwaambia watu waketi chini kwenye nyasi. Akachukua mikate mitano na samaki wawili, akatazama mbinguni, akamshukuru Mungu kwa ajili ya chakula. Kisha akaimega mikate vipande vipande, akawapa wanafunzi. Wanafunzi wakawapa watu chakula.

vi.L: Và sau khi truyền cho đoàn dân ngồi trên cỏ, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cầm lấy năm cái bánh và hai con cá, ngước mắt lên trời mà chúc phước, rồi bẻ ra và trao bánh cho các môn đồ, còn các môn đồ [trao] cho đoàn dân.
vi.B: Ngài bảo dân chúng ngồi xuống trên cỏ. Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cầm lấy năm cái bánh và hai con cá, ngước mắt lên trời và dâng lời chúc tụng. Ngài bẻ bánh ra, trao cho các môn đồ, và các môn đồ phân phát cho dân chúng.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu bảo dân chúng ngồi xuống trên cỏ. Ngài cầm lấy năm cái bánh và hai con cá, rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nhìn lên trời và cảm tạ Đức Chúa Trời về thức ăn. Sau đó {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bẻ bánh ra thành từng miếng và trao cho các môn đồ. Các môn đồ phân phát thức ăn cho dân chúng.

decisions.choice: blessed: praised God over the food
decisions.reason: A Jewish meal began with a blessing of God, who brings bread from the earth. The verb has no object here, so the praise is given to God.

decisions.choice: took, blessed, broke, gave: the actions of the Last Supper
alternatives: ordinary actions at a meal with no further meaning
decisions.reason: Matthew uses the same four verbs when Jesus takes the bread at the Last Supper (26:26), and again at the second feeding (15:36).

decisions.choice: recline: lie down to eat, as at a meal
decisions.reason: People reclined to eat at a proper meal. Here the crowd is seated as guests at a meal Jesus provides.

decisions.choice: looked up to heaven: a gesture of prayer
alternatives: looked at the sky to judge the time
decisions.reason: People often prayed with eyes lifted toward heaven, God's dwelling (Psalm 123:1).

decisions.choice: sit down
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the posture readers picture, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: thanked God for the food
decisions.reason: Readable says to whom the blessing was spoken. Literal and Balanced keep the word "blessed".

decisions.choice: waegemee (L); waketi (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is to recline as at a meal (meaning decision m3). "Kuegemea" keeps the posture at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "sit", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "chúc phước" (L); "dâng lời chúc tụng" (B); "cảm tạ Đức Chúa Trời về thức ăn" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 6:41: Jesus praises God over the food (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "ngồi" for reclining
decisions.reason: People lay down to eat at a meal (meaning decision); Vietnamese, like the English, says "sit", the posture readers picture at a meal.

source.text: καὶ ἔφαγον πάντες καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν, καὶ ἦραν τὸ περισσεῦον τῶν κλασμάτων δώδεκα κοφίνους πλήρεις.

records.literal_gloss: And ate all and were satisfied, and they took up that being over and above of the fragments twelve baskets full.

en.L: And all ate and were satisfied, and they picked up what was left over of the broken pieces, twelve baskets full.
en.B: Everyone ate and had enough. Then they collected what remained of the broken pieces, and it filled twelve baskets.
en.R: All of the people ate as much as they wanted. After that, the followers gathered up the pieces of food that were left. They filled twelve baskets with them.

es.L: Y comieron todos y quedaron satisfechos, y levantaron de los pedazos lo sobrante: doce cestas llenas.
es.B: Todos comieron hasta quedar satisfechos. Después juntaron los pedazos que habían quedado, y llenaron doce cestas.
es.R: Toda la gente comió todo lo que quiso. Después, los seguidores recogieron los pedazos de comida que sobraron. Llenaron doce cestas con ellos.

fr.L: Et tous mangèrent et furent rassasiés, et ils ramassèrent ce qui restait des morceaux, douze paniers pleins.
fr.B: Tout le monde mangea à sa faim. Puis on ramassa les morceaux qui restaient, et on en remplit douze paniers.
fr.R: Tout le monde a mangé autant qu’il voulait. Après cela, les disciples ont ramassé les morceaux qui restaient. Ils en ont rempli douze paniers.

sw.L: Na wote wakala wakashiba, nao wakaokota kilichobaki cha vipande, vikapu kumi na viwili vilivyojaa.
sw.B: Kila mtu alikula, akashiba. Kisha wakakusanya vipande vilivyobaki, navyo vikajaza vikapu kumi na viwili.
sw.R: Watu wote walikula kadiri walivyotaka. Baadaye wanafunzi wakaokota vipande vya chakula vilivyobaki. Wakajaza vikapu kumi na viwili.

vi.L: Và mọi người đều ăn và được no nê, rồi người ta nhặt những mẩu bánh còn thừa, được mười hai giỏ đầy.
vi.B: Mọi người đều ăn no. Rồi các môn đồ nhặt những mẩu bánh còn thừa, được đầy mười hai giỏ.
vi.R: Ai cũng được ăn bao nhiêu tùy thích. Sau đó, các môn đồ nhặt những miếng bánh còn thừa. Họ đựng đầy mười hai giỏ.

decisions.choice: were satisfied: were filled, had all they wanted
decisions.reason: The verb means to be fed until full. God gives his people bread until they are satisfied (Psalm 132:15).

decisions.choice: baskets: hand baskets of wicker
decisions.reason: This basket is the kind carried by hand. At the second feeding Matthew uses a different word for a larger basket (15:37; 16:9-10).

decisions.choice: twelve: one basket for each of the Twelve
alternatives: a symbol of the twelve tribes
decisions.reason: There is a basketful for each disciple who served the crowd. Some see a hint of the twelve tribes of Israel. The plain point is that more was left over than was there at the start.

decisions.choice: the followers
decisions.reason: Readable names who gathered the pieces. The disciples served the food (14:19) and would gather what was left; Matthew does not say so here.

decisions.choice: "các môn đồ" (B, R); "người ta" (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "they"; Balanced and Readable name the disciples, as the English Readable does, since they serve the food in 14:19.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἐσθίοντες ἦσαν ἄνδρες ὡσεὶ πεντακισχίλιοι χωρὶς γυναικῶν καὶ παιδίων.

records.literal_gloss: Those then eating were men about five thousand besides women and children.

en.L: And those who ate were about 5,000 men, besides women and children.
en.B: The men who ate numbered about 5,000, not counting women and children.
en.R: About 5,000 men ate the food. Women and children ate too, but they were not counted.

es.L: Y los que comían eran hombres, como 5000, aparte de mujeres y niños.
es.B: Los hombres que comieron eran unos 5000, sin contar a mujeres y niños.
es.R: Unos 5000 hombres comieron. También comieron mujeres y niños, pero a ellos no los contaron.

fr.L: Or ceux qui avaient mangé étaient environ 5 000 hommes, sans compter les femmes et les enfants.
fr.B: Les hommes qui avaient mangé étaient au nombre d’environ 5 000, sans compter les femmes et les enfants.
fr.R: Environ 5 000 hommes ont mangé. Les femmes et les enfants ont mangé aussi, mais on ne les a pas comptés.

sw.L: Basi wale waliokuwa wakila walikuwa wanaume kama elfu tano, mbali na wanawake na watoto.
sw.B: Wanaume waliokula walikuwa karibu elfu tano, bila kuhesabu wanawake na watoto.
sw.R: Wanaume wapatao elfu tano walikula chakula. Wanawake na watoto pia walikula, lakini hawakuhesabiwa.

vi.L: Và những người đã ăn là khoảng năm nghìn người đàn ông, không kể phụ nữ và trẻ em.
vi.B: Số đàn ông đã ăn là khoảng năm nghìn người, không kể phụ nữ và trẻ em.
vi.R: Có khoảng năm nghìn người đàn ông đã ăn. Phụ nữ và trẻ em cũng ăn, nhưng không được đếm.

decisions.choice: men: adult males
decisions.reason: The word here means men as distinct from women and children, who are named next. The men were counted; the whole crowd was larger.

decisions.choice: besides women and children: they were there but not counted
alternatives: there were no women and children
decisions.reason: Matthew alone mentions them, here and at 15:38. Crowds were counted by the men.
Numbers above ninety-nine are written as numerals, as at Acts 4:4.

decisions.choice: hombres, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The Greek word here means adult males, the ones who were counted (meaning decision m1), so "hombres" is not under the setting, as in John 6:10. Spanish writes four-digit numbers without a separator.

decisions.choice: 5 000, in figures with a narrow no-break space
decisions.reason: As at Mark 6:44: numbers above "cent" are in figures, grouped with a space as French does. "Hommes" takes no gender setting, because only the men were counted (m1).

decisions.choice: wanaume
decisions.reason: The Greek word here means adult males, the ones who were counted (meaning decision m1), so Swahili says "wanaume", as in John 6:10, and not the general "watu".

decisions.choice: "năm nghìn" in words
decisions.reason: As in Mark 6:44: the style guide writes numbers in words in running text, where the English uses figures.
